Gson Deserialization Flow: From API to Token Reading

This document traces the complete deserialization flow when application code calls gson.fromJson(json, MyType.class). The flow shows the internal steps and real classes/methods involved, from the public entry point down to where JSON characters are actually read from the input stream.

1. Public API Entry Point

Application Code

MyType obj = gson.fromJson(jsonString, MyType.class);

Gson.fromJson(String, Class) — Line 850

2. Type Wrapping

Creates a TypeToken<T> instance that captures the generic type information.

public <T> T fromJson(String json, TypeToken<T> typeOfT) { if (json == null) return null; StringReader reader = new StringReader(json); return fromJson(reader, typeOfT); }

Action: Wraps the JSON string in a StringReader (standard Java Reader) and delegates to the Reader overload.

3. Reader Creation and JsonReader Instantiation

Gson.fromJson(Reader, TypeToken) — Line 1001

public <T> T fromJson(Reader json, TypeToken<T> typeOfT) { JsonReader jsonReader = newJsonReader(json); T object = fromJson(jsonReader, typeOfT); assertFullConsumption(object, jsonReader); return object; }

Action: Creates a JsonReader from the underlying Java Reader.

Gson.newJsonReader(Reader) — Line 821

public JsonReader newJsonReader(Reader reader) { JsonReader jsonReader = new JsonReader(reader); jsonReader.setStrictness(strictness == null ? Strictness.LEGACY_STRICT : strictness); return jsonReader; }

4. Core Deserialization Dispatch

Gson.fromJson(JsonReader, TypeToken) — Line 1087

public <T> T fromJson(JsonReader reader, TypeToken<T> typeOfT) { boolean isEmpty = true; try { JsonToken unused = reader.peek(); // <-- Peeks at first token isEmpty = false; TypeAdapter<T> typeAdapter = getAdapter(typeOfT); // <-- Gets adapter T object = typeAdapter.read(reader); // <-- Calls adapter's read() // Type safety check Class<?> expectedTypeWrapped = Primitives.wrap(typeOfT.getRawType()); if (object != null && !expectedTypeWrapped.isInstance(object)) { throw new ClassCastException(...); } return object; } catch (EOFException e) { if (isEmpty) return null; throw new JsonSyntaxException(e); } }

  2. Retrieves the appropriate TypeAdapter for the target type

5. Type Adapter Selection

Gson.getAdapter(TypeToken) — Line 340

public <T> TypeAdapter<T> getAdapter(TypeToken<T> type) { // Check cache first TypeAdapter<?> cached = typeTokenCache.get(type); if (cached != null) return (TypeAdapter<T>) cached; // Iterate through registered TypeAdapterFactory instances for (TypeAdapterFactory factory : factories) { TypeAdapter<T> candidate = factory.create(this, type); if (candidate != null) { typeTokenCache.put(type, candidate); return candidate; } } throw new IllegalArgumentException("GSON cannot handle " + type); }

  • Collections and Maps
  • Enums and Dates

Adapter.read(JsonReader) — Line 503

@Override public T read(JsonReader in) throws IOException { if (in.peek() == JsonToken.NULL) { in.nextNull(); return null; } A accumulator = createAccumulator(); // Create empty object Map<String, BoundField> deserializedFields = fieldsData.deserializedFields; in.beginObject(); // Expects '{' while (in.hasNext()) { String name = in.nextName(); // Reads field name BoundField field = deserializedFields.get(name); if (field == null) { in.skipValue(); // Unknown field } else { readField(accumulator, in, field); // Deserialize field value } } in.endObject(); // Expects '}' return finalize(accumulator); // Return populated object }

  5. Reads } token via endObject()

7. JsonReader: Token Peeking and Consumption

Component Purpose
Reader in Underlying Java Reader (from StringReader → InputStream, etc.)

public JsonToken peek() throws IOException { int p = peeked; if (p == PEEKED_NONE) { p = doPeek(); // Perform lexical analysis } switch (p) { case PEEKED_BEGIN_OBJECT: return JsonToken.BEGIN_OBJECT; // '{' case PEEKED_END_OBJECT: return JsonToken.END_OBJECT; // '}' case PEEKED_BEGIN_ARRAY: return JsonToken.BEGIN_ARRAY; // '[' case PEEKED_END_ARRAY: return JsonToken.END_ARRAY; // ']' case PEEKED_NULL: return JsonToken.NULL; // null case PEEKED_TRUE: return JsonToken.BOOLEAN; // true case PEEKED_FALSE: return JsonToken.BOOLEAN; // false case PEEKED_SINGLE_QUOTED_NAME: case PEEKED_DOUBLE_QUOTED_NAME: case PEEKED_UNQUOTED_NAME: return JsonToken.NAME; // field name case PEEKED_SINGLE_QUOTED: case PEEKED_DOUBLE_QUOTED: case PEEKED_UNQUOTED: case PEEKED_BUFFERED: return JsonToken.STRING; // string value case PEEKED_LONG: case PEEKED_NUMBER: return JsonToken.NUMBER; // number case PEEKED_EOF: return JsonToken.END_DOCUMENT; // end } }

Action: Returns a JsonToken enum value representing the next token type without consuming it.

JsonReader.doPeek() — Line 582 (State Machine)

This is the core lexical analyzer. It reads characters from the buffer and identifies JSON structure:

int doPeek() throws IOException { int peekStack = stack[stackSize - 1]; if (peekStack == JsonScope.EMPTY_ARRAY) { // In an array: look for ']' or ',' int c = nextNonWhitespace(true); switch (c) { case ']': peeked = PEEKED_END_ARRAY; return peeked; case ',': /* continue parsing next value */ } } else if (peekStack == JsonScope.EMPTY_OBJECT || peekStack == JsonScope.NONEMPTY_OBJECT) { // In an object: look for field name or '}' int c = nextNonWhitespace(true); switch (c) { case '"': peeked = PEEKED_DOUBLE_QUOTED_NAME; return peeked; case '\'': peeked = PEEKED_SINGLE_QUOTED_NAME; return peeked; case '}': peeked = PEEKED_END_OBJECT; return peeked; default: peeked = PEEKED_UNQUOTED_NAME; return peeked; } } else if (peekStack == JsonScope.DANGLING_NAME) { // After field name: look for ':' int c = nextNonWhitespace(true); if (c != ':') throw syntaxError("Expected ':'"); } // ... continues with value parsing (true, false, null, numbers, strings) }

Key Points: The method uses a stack to track context (object/array nesting) and identifies JSON structural elements by reading individual characters.

When doPeek() needs more input and the buffer is exhausted, it calls fillBuffer(), which is where JSON characters are actually read from the underlying Java Reader.

JsonReader.fillBuffer(minimum) — Line 1512

private boolean fillBuffer(int minimum) throws IOException { char[] buffer = this.buffer; // 1024-char array // Shift unconsumed data to start of buffer lineStart -= pos; if (limit != pos) { limit -= pos; System.arraycopy(buffer, pos, buffer, 0, limit); } else { limit = 0; } pos = 0; int total; // <-- ACTUAL READING HAPPENS HERE while ((total = in.read(buffer, limit, buffer.length - limit)) != -1) { limit += total; // Skip BOM if this is the first read if (lineNumber == 0 && lineStart == 0 && limit > 0 && buffer[0] == '﻿') { pos++; lineStart++; minimum++; } if (limit >= minimum) { return true; // Enough data available } } return false; // End of stream }

The Critical Line: in.read(buffer, limit, buffer.length - limit) reads from the underlying Reader into the char array buffer. This is where JSON characters flow into memory.

Flow:

  • Shifts any unconsumed characters in the buffer to the start
  • Calls in.read() (the Java Reader) to fill the rest of the buffer
  • Tracks line numbers and handles UTF-8 BOM
  • Returns true if enough data was read, false at EOF

9. Parsing String Values

When a string token is encountered, JsonReader parses it character-by-character from the buffer:

JsonReader.nextQuotedValue(quote) — Line 1141

private String nextQuotedValue(char quote) throws IOException { char[] buffer = this.buffer; StringBuilder builder = null; while (true) { int p = pos; int l = limit; int start = p; // Read characters until closing quote or escape sequence while (p < l) { int c = buffer[p++]; if (c == quote) { // Found closing quote pos = p; int len = p - start - 1; if (builder == null) { return new String(buffer, start, len); // Simple case: no escapes } else { builder.append(buffer, start, len); return builder.toString(); } } else if (c == '\\\\') { // Handle escape sequence pos = p; int len = p - start - 1; if (builder == null) { builder = new StringBuilder((len + 1) * 2); } builder.append(buffer, start, len); builder.append(readEscapeCharacter()); // Parse \n, \t, \uXXXX, etc. p = pos; l = limit; start = p; } else if (c == '\\n') { lineNumber++; lineStart = p; } } // Buffer exhausted before closing quote if (builder == null) { builder = new StringBuilder(16); } builder.append(buffer, start, p - start); if (!fillBuffer(1)) { throw syntaxError("Unterminated string"); } } }

Key Points:

  • Reads characters directly from the internal buffer char array
  • Handles escape sequences (\\n, \\t, \\u1234, etc.) via readEscapeCharacter()
  • Constructs the string incrementally, calling fillBuffer() if it reaches buffer end mid-string
  • Tracks line numbers for error reporting

10. Number Parsing

Numbers are parsed by reading digits and determining type (long vs. double), then parsed into Java primitives:

// Example flow for a number like 123 or 45.67 // 1. doPeek() identifies it as PEEKED_NUMBER or PEEKED_LONG // 2. nextInt() / nextLong() / nextDouble() extract digits from buffer // 3. Java's Long.parseLong() / Double.parseDouble() converts to Java number

Complete Call Stack Example

For deserializing a JSON object like {"name":"Alice","age":30} to a Person class:

gson.fromJson(jsonString, Person.class) ├─ TypeToken.get(Person.class) └─ gson.fromJson(jsonString, TypeToken<Person>) ├─ new StringReader(jsonString) └─ gson.fromJson(StringReader, TypeToken<Person>) ├─ newJsonReader(StringReader) │ └─ new JsonReader(StringReader) └─ gson.fromJson(JsonReader, TypeToken<Person>) ├─ reader.peek() │ └─ doPeek() │ └─ fillBuffer(1) │ └─ in.read(buffer, limit, size) [actual I/O] ├─ getAdapter(TypeToken<Person>) │ └─ ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory.create() │ └─ new FieldReflectionAdapter(...) └─ typeAdapter.read(JsonReader) ├─ reader.beginObject() // '{' │ └─ reader.peek() / doPeek() ├─ Loop: while (reader.hasNext()) │ ├─ reader.nextName() │ │ └─ reader.nextQuotedValue('"') │ │ └─ reads "name" from buffer, calls fillBuffer() if needed │ └─ field.readIntoField(reader, accumulator) │ └─ TypeAdapter<String>.read(reader) [for "name" field] │ └─ reader.nextString() → nextQuotedValue('"') │ └─ reads "Alice" from buffer │ │ ├─ reader.nextName() → "age" │ └─ TypeAdapter<Integer>.read(reader) │ └─ reader.nextInt() │ └─ parses 30 from buffer └─ reader.endObject() // '}'

Key Internal Classes Summary

Class Purpose Key Methods
Gson Public API entry point; coordinates factories and adapters fromJson(), getAdapter()
TypeAdapter<T> Abstract base for type-specific serialization/deserialization logic read(JsonReader), write(JsonWriter)
TypeAdapterFactory Creates TypeAdapters for specific types (chain of responsibility pattern) create(Gson, TypeToken)
ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory Factory for custom POJOs using reflection create() → FieldReflectionAdapter
Adapter<T, A> Base class for reflection-based adapters (internal to ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory) read(JsonReader), write(JsonWriter)
JsonReader Lexical analyzer and token stream; reads from underlying Java Reader peek(), nextName(), nextString(), nextInt(), beginObject(), endObject(), fillBuffer()
JsonToken Enum representing JSON structural tokens and value types BEGIN_OBJECT, NAME, STRING, NUMBER, NULL, END_OBJECT, etc.

The Core Loop: Token → Value Extraction

The essence of Gson's deserialization is this repeated pattern:

  1. Peek: Call reader.peek() to identify the next token type without consuming it
  2. Route: Based on token type, call the appropriate reader.nextXxx() method
  3. Extract: The nextXxx() method reads characters from the buffer (calling fillBuffer() as needed) and returns the parsed Java value
  4. Recurse: For objects and arrays, delegate to nested TypeAdapters to deserialize sub-values

Performance Optimization: Buffering

JsonReader's design is optimized for performance:

  • Circular buffer: 1024-character window reuses memory; data is shifted, not copied
  • Lazy lexing: doPeek() only analyzes as far as needed to identify the next token
  • Cache: Once a token is peeked, it's cached in the peeked flag; no re-analysis until consumed
  • Direct string construction: For strings without escape sequences, new String(buffer, start, len) avoids extra copying

Summary

Gson's deserialization architecture is a layered pipeline:

Public API (String/Reader/JsonReader input)
↓
Gson: Type Adapter Lookup & Dispatch
↓
TypeAdapter: Type-Specific Deserialization Logic
↓
JsonReader: Lexical Analysis & Token Stream
↓
JsonReader.fillBuffer() / Reader.read(): Actual I/O
↓
Parsed Java Object

Each layer handles one responsibility: type resolution, deserialization logic, tokenization, and I/O. The JsonReader is the heart, maintaining a sliding window buffer and reading JSON characters from the underlying stream on demand, enabling efficient streaming deserialization without loading the entire JSON into a tree structure (unless explicitly using the tree API).

private String nextQuotedValue(char quote) throws IOException { char[] buffer = this.buffer; StringBuilder builder = null; while (true) { int p = pos; int l = limit; int start = p; // Read characters until closing quote or escape sequence while (p < l) { int c = buffer[p++]; if (c == quote) { // Found closing quote pos = p; int len = p - start - 1; if (builder == null) { return new String(buffer, start, len); // Simple case: no escapes } else { builder.append(buffer, start, len); return builder.toString(); } } else if (c == '\\\\') { // Handle escape sequence pos = p; int len = p - start - 1; if (builder == null) { builder = new StringBuilder((len + 1) * 2); } builder.append(buffer, start, len); builder.append(readEscapeCharacter()); // Parse \n, \t, \uXXXX, etc. p = pos; l = limit; start = p; } else if (c == '\\n') { lineNumber++; lineStart = p; } } // Buffer exhausted before closing quote if (builder == null) { builder = new StringBuilder(16); } builder.append(buffer, start, p - start); if (!fillBuffer(1)) { throw syntaxError("Unterminated string"); } } }

Key Points:

  • Reads characters directly from the internal buffer char array
  • Handles escape sequences (\\n, \\t, \\u1234, etc.) via readEscapeCharacter()
  • Constructs the string incrementally, calling fillBuffer() if it reaches buffer end mid-string
  • Tracks line numbers for error reporting

10. Number Parsing

Numbers are parsed by reading digits and determining type (long vs. double), then parsed into Java primitives:

// Example flow for a number like 123 or 45.67 // 1. doPeek() identifies it as PEEKED_NUMBER or PEEKED_LONG // 2. nextInt() / nextLong() / nextDouble() extract digits from buffer // 3. Java's Long.parseLong() / Double.parseDouble() converts to Java number

Complete Call Stack Example

For deserializing a JSON object like {"name":"Alice","age":30} to a Person class:

gson.fromJson(jsonString, Person.class) ├─ TypeToken.get(Person.class) └─ gson.fromJson(jsonString, TypeToken<Person>) ├─ new StringReader(jsonString) └─ gson.fromJson(StringReader, TypeToken<Person>) ├─ newJsonReader(StringReader) │ └─ new JsonReader(StringReader) └─ gson.fromJson(JsonReader, TypeToken<Person>) ├─ reader.peek() │ └─ doPeek() │ └─ fillBuffer(1) │ └─ in.read(buffer, limit, size) [actual I/O] ├─ getAdapter(TypeToken<Person>) │ └─ ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory.create() │ └─ new FieldReflectionAdapter(...) └─ typeAdapter.read(JsonReader) ├─ reader.beginObject() // '{' │ └─ reader.peek() / doPeek() ├─ Loop: while (reader.hasNext()) │ ├─ reader.nextName() │ │ └─ reader.nextQuotedValue('"') │ │ └─ reads "name" from buffer, calls fillBuffer() if needed │ └─ field.readIntoField(reader, accumulator) │ └─ TypeAdapter<String>.read(reader) [for "name" field] │ └─ reader.nextString() → nextQuotedValue('"') │ └─ reads "Alice" from buffer │ │ ├─ reader.nextName() → "age" │ └─ TypeAdapter<Integer>.read(reader) │ └─ reader.nextInt() │ └─ parses 30 from buffer └─ reader.endObject() // '}'

Key Internal Classes Summary

Class Purpose Key Methods
Gson Public API entry point; coordinates factories and adapters fromJson(), getAdapter()
TypeAdapter<T> Abstract base for type-specific serialization/deserialization logic read(JsonReader), write(JsonWriter)
TypeAdapterFactory Creates TypeAdapters for specific types (chain of responsibility pattern) create(Gson, TypeToken)
ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory Factory for custom POJOs using reflection create() → FieldReflectionAdapter
Adapter<T, A> Base class for reflection-based adapters (internal to ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory) read(JsonReader), write(JsonWriter)
JsonReader Lexical analyzer and token stream; reads from underlying Java Reader peek(), nextName(), nextString(), nextInt(), beginObject(), endObject(), fillBuffer()
JsonToken Enum representing JSON structural tokens and value types BEGIN_OBJECT, NAME, STRING, NUMBER, NULL, END_OBJECT, etc.

The Core Loop: Token → Value Extraction

The essence of Gson's deserialization is this repeated pattern:

  1. Peek: Call reader.peek() to identify the next token type without consuming it
  2. Route: Based on token type, call the appropriate reader.nextXxx() method
  3. Extract: The nextXxx() method reads characters from the buffer (calling fillBuffer() as needed) and returns the parsed Java value
  4. Recurse: For objects and arrays, delegate to nested TypeAdapters to deserialize sub-values

Performance Optimization: Buffering

JsonReader's design is optimized for performance:

  • Circular buffer: 1024-character window reuses memory; data is shifted, not copied
  • Lazy lexing: doPeek() only analyzes as far as needed to identify the next token
  • Cache: Once a token is peeked, it's cached in the peeked flag; no re-analysis until consumed
  • Direct string construction: For strings without escape sequences, new String(buffer, start, len) avoids extra copying

Summary

Gson's deserialization architecture is a layered pipeline:

Public API (String/Reader/JsonReader input)
↓
Gson: Type Adapter Lookup & Dispatch
↓
TypeAdapter: Type-Specific Deserialization Logic
↓
JsonReader: Lexical Analysis & Token Stream
↓
JsonReader.fillBuffer() / Reader.read(): Actual I/O
↓
Parsed Java Object

Each layer handles one responsibility: type resolution, deserialization logic, tokenization, and I/O. The JsonReader is the heart, maintaining a sliding window buffer and reading JSON characters from the underlying stream on demand, enabling efficient streaming deserialization without loading the entire JSON into a tree structure (unless explicitly using the tree API).

Perfect! I've created a comprehensive walkthrough of Gson's deserialization flow. Here's a summary of the internal steps:

## Key Findings: The Deserialization Pipeline

**When you call `gson.fromJson(json, MyType.class)`, here's what happens:**

1. **Entry Point** → `Gson.fromJson(String, Class)` wraps the class in a `TypeToken`

2. **Reader Setup** → Creates a `StringReader` and passes it to `Gson.fromJson(Reader, TypeToken)`, which instantiates a `JsonReader` via `newJsonReader()`

3. **Adapter Lookup** → `Gson.getAdapter(TypeToken)` iterates through a chain of `TypeAdapterFactory` instances to find/create a `TypeAdapter` for your type. For custom objects, `ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory` creates a `FieldReflectionAdapter`

4. **Deserialization Dispatch** → Core method `Gson.fromJson(JsonReader, TypeToken)` calls `typeAdapter.read(reader)` — the type-specific deserialization logic

5. **Object Reflection** → `Adapter.read(JsonReader)` (for POJOs):
   - Calls `reader.beginObject()` to consume `{`
   - Loops through object members, reading field names via `reader.nextName()`
   - For each field, delegates to nested TypeAdapters to deserialize values
   - Calls `reader.endObject()` to consume `}`

6. **Token Reading** → `JsonReader.peek()` identifies the next token type by calling `doPeek()`:
   - **doPeek()** is a state machine that reads characters and identifies JSON structure (`{`, `}`, `[`, `]`, strings, numbers, `null`, `true`, `false`)
   - It uses an internal `int[] stack` to track nesting context
   - Caches the identified token type in the `peeked` flag

7. **Character I/O** → When `doPeek()` or value-parsing methods need more input:
   - **fillBuffer()** is called
   - It reads from the underlying `Reader` via `in.read(buffer, limit, size)` — **this is where JSON characters actually flow into memory**
   - Uses a 1024-character circular buffer for efficiency

8. **String Parsing** → `nextQuotedValue(quote)` reads string characters from the buffer:
   - Scans the buffer char-by-char until closing quote
   - Handles escape sequences (`\n`, `\t`, `\uXXXX`) via `readEscapeCharacter()`
   - Calls `fillBuffer()` if it runs out of buffered data mid-string
   - Constructs the string result

**The real classes involved:**
- `Gson` — public API and factory coordination
- `TypeAdapter<T>` — abstract base for deserialization logic
- `TypeAdapterFactory` — creates adapters (chain pattern)
- `ReflectiveTypeAdapterFactory` / `Adapter` — POJO deserialization via reflection
- `JsonReader` — lexical analyzer with buffered token stream
- `JsonToken` — enum representing token types

I've published a detailed interactive guide as an artifact showing the complete call stack, code snippets, and architecture. Check the link above for the full walkthrough with examples and diagrams!
